question.text: Under SEBI (CAPSM) Regulations, which factors does SEBI consider when deciding which associated persons need certification?

answer.text: All of: whether the person deals or interacts with investors, issuers or clients; handles assets or funds of investors or clients; handles investor grievance redressal; is responsible for internal control, risk management or compliance; and undertakes activities bearing on operational risk
Whether the person deals or interacts with investors, issuers, or clients
Whether the person handles assets or funds of investors or clients
Whether the person is responsible for internal control, risk management, or compliance

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 3(4) of the SEBI (CAPSM) Regulations, SEBI considers a comprehensive set of factors: (a) interaction with investors, issuers or clients; (b) dealing with assets or funds of investors/clients; (c) handling investor grievance redressal; (d) responsibility for internal control or risk management; (e) responsibility for compliance; and (f) activities bearing on operational risk. The correct option captures all of these factors. The Trap: Each single-factor distractor is true on its own, which tempts a candidate to stop there. SEBI applies a comprehensive view, so any role that touches one or more of these factors may bring the associated person within the certification requirement. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone option that lists the full set of CAPSM factors, and removed the pro-tip line that was not source-grounded.
